transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-30
Start time: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: All-hands (virtual)
Attendees: Leadership + company-wide

Auto-generated summary: Leadership gave a high-level on Q2 wins, callouts on reliability improvements, product priorities for Q3, and org updates. Several questions on pricing, private deployments, and hiring timelines.

[00:00] Alex (CEO): hey everyone, thanks for joining. happy to see so many faces. okay we'll kick off, quick agenda — Q2 recap, roadmap highlights, ops/reliability, people updates and then q and a. we'll try to keep it tight.
[00:35] Priya (CTO): good morning all. quick engineering call out: we're seeing a 22% reduction in median p99 latencies on the hosted API since the kernel selection changes rolled out in early june. there's still tail work, but big thanks to the infra team. note: some of the numbers vary by model and seq length, so look at the perf dashboard in the console.
[01:10] Marcus (VP Eng): yeah to add, the continuous batching release helped throughput by about 18% for customer workloads with bursty traffic. small caveat — we saw a spike in queuing in a small set of dedicated clusters last week, part of that was an autoscaling tuning mismatch. we've patched and have a follow-up runbook.
[01:45] Alex: awesome. quick numbers: revenue growth QoQ is in the mid-30% range, usage growth driven by new PLG signups and a couple of midmarket expansions. churn is stable. these are preliminary numbers — finance will share the deck later.
[02:20] Sofia (Head of Product): roadmap highlights — Dedicated capacity improvements, full Private control-plane beta for a couple of customers, and Redwood Optimize 1.1 (cost/perf suggestions + quantization guidance). for q3 we want to focus on rollout tooling and better model variant routing so customers can failover to cheaper variants automatically.
[03:05] Alex: one thing i want to call out, the private deployments are a big strategic play for us. we have to be careful about operational burden though, so we're standardizing the CNC and packaging.
[03:30] Dana (Head of People): hiring update — we're about 18 hires this quarter across eng, product, and customer success. emphasis on SRE and infra work. we're also experimenting with a referral bonus tweak to pull more senior infra folks. we expect slower ramp times so managers please plan for that in roadmaps.
[04:05] Jamal (Sales): customer momentum — closed 3 reserved capacity deals this month, notable wins in fintech and health. customers asked specifically about SOC2 scope and audit readiness; we've been handing out the security one-pager.
[04:40] Lina (CS): also seeing more requests for private networking (V P C) and key-management integrations. a few customers asked about on-prem options as well. we need better materials to guide those conversions.
[05:10] Audience question (Employee 1): what's the timeline for the Private GA?
[05:20] Sofia: good Q — we're targeting GA for a limited set in Q3, broadly later in Q4 depending on feedback. the beta customers will drive the last mile work on installation and KMS integrations.
[05:45] Priya: technical caveat — private brings a lot of variability: customer hardware, network configs, and of course H S M integrations. the runtime has to be more defensive. expect performance profiles to vary more vs hosted.
[06:20] Alex: on the pricing front, we're experimenting with a clearer tradeoff menu — documented guidance on latency vs cost, and recommended model/quantization profiles for common workloads.
[06:50] Marcus: ops update — we've been investing in KV cache improvements which reduced repeated token cost in several customer prompts. note: in some transcriptions KV cache was misheard as "KV cash" — but it's cache. also we've improved prefix caching to reduce cold-starts.
[07:30] Erik (SRE): incident recap — we had an outage impacting a small customer shard last week; root cause was a mis-applied autoscale policy combined with a driver regression on one GPU type. rollback and a fix were applied within 47 minutes. postmortem is on the runbook page.
[08:05] Alex: thanks erik. overall we want fewer of these. the SLA focus remains a top priority for enterprise deals.
[08:30] Dana: culture note — we hear about burnout on some teams after the push in may. managers, please review load and make use of the extra flex days program. starting july we'll pilot a 4-day focused sprint for a couple of teams.
[09:00] Audience question (Employee 2): will the 4-day pilot affect hiring timelines?
[09:10] Dana: no, hiring continues as planned; pilot is just to experiment with focus/time-off. hiring managers should still plan ramp in their milestones.
[09:35] Sofia: product question from slack — can we get more granular cost recommendations in Optimize per route? yes, that's on the roadmap for 1.2; we want to show per-route token breakdowns and suggested quantization.
[10:05] Marcus: on autoscaler — we're adding a simulator for scale policies so teams can test before rolling out. this should cut surprises.
[10:35] Alex: ok quick customer highlight — finance customer Y took Redwood Dedicated and saw a 2.5x improvement in throughput for their specific reconciliation workload after we tuned kernels for that model family. little shout out to the kernel team.
[11:00] Priya: on the research front, we're continuing work on attention optimizations and some kernel fusions that look promising. those may move into the runtime later this quarter.
[11:25] Jamal: sales ask — we need case studies and a clean reference list for the midmarket. marketing and cs, let's coordinate.
[11:45] Lina: noted, we'll draft one by next week and share a template.
[12:05] Audience question (Employee 3): what about competitors — are we seeing pressure on price?
[12:20] Alex: yes, some customers mention lower-cost endpoints elsewhere. our answer is predictable performance + tooling + support. we also have Optimize to help lower unit costs. we should be pragmatic — where it makes sense, route by cost and region.
[12:55] Audience question (Employee 4): will there be changes to compensation / equity given growth?
[13:10] Dana: we do a regular refresh cycle; nothing immediate to announce. we'll share the compensation cadence in the next all-hands.
[13:35] Alex: quick logistics — company retreat in september, please watch the invite; we'll do working groups on product, reliability, and customer success. dana will open signups.
[13:55] Priya: last tech note — we're starting an internal perf benchmark program to publish reproducible fixtures so customers can compare. it'll include model families, seq lengths, and hardware labeled clearly. please contribute sample workloads.
[14:20] Alex: ok wrapping up. thanks everyone. quick recap of action items — roadmap doc, incident runbook, retreat working groups, customer references.
[14:40] Q&A continues with a few rapid fire questions about vacation policy and hiring comp bands, then meeting ends around 11:02 AM UTC.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels collapsed; some product names and acronyms were auto-transcribed imperfectly (e.g., "V P C" instead of VPC, "KV cash" instead of KV cache). For full accuracy, refer to posted recording and docs.
